On 25 April 2025, students and citizens gathered in front of the Radio Television of Serbia (RTS) premises across Belgrade, blocking the entrances in protest against the spread of disinformation and supporting the regime narratives. Citizens also supported and sent off the marathon runners in their endeavour to reach Brussels to voice the students' demands to the political authorities in the European Union. Furthermore, an individual attempted to run through the crowd with a car but was prevented by the police.

On 25 April 2025, high-school and faculty students Jagodina from marching towards Novi Sad arrived in Lapovo, where they were welcomed by the local population and spent the night before continuing their march. Students from all over Serbia will gather in Novi Sad to demand accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 25 April 2025, citizens marched through Leskovac, observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign and making loud noises as a protest against the government's usage of Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) during the Belgrade protests on 15 March.

On 25 April 2025, students and citizens gathered in Novi Sad, demanding accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. Citizens also supported and sent off the marathon runners in their endeavour to reach Brussels to voice the students' demands to the political authorities in the European Union.

On 25 April 2025, several tens of students and citizens gathered and blocked the entrance in front of the Faculty for Sports and Physical Education in Novi Sad, protesting against the lack of responsiveness and support from the Faculty's management to the students' demands. The protesters also condemned the Faculty dean's actions, who broke the blockade and violently entered the building, by kicking one student's leg earlier.

On 25 April 2025, Russian and Ukrainian military clashed near Andriivka, Donetsk. The Russian military lost 137 soldiers, 65 of them irreversibly, near Yelyzavetivka, Preobrazhenka, Andriivka, Stara Mykolaivka, Lysivka, Kotlyne, Novooleksandrivka, Myroliubivka, Romanivka, Malynivka (65 fatalities split across 10 events and coded as 7).

Agreement: On 19 April 2025, Vladimir Putin announced the Easter Sunday ceasefire (coded as Moscow). The verbal ceasefire was supposed to be in place since 18:00 19th April to 00:00 21st April (Moscow time). The statement was made public only a few hours before the ceasefire was supposed to begin, and the sudden nature of the announcement, by many accounts, was supposed to catch Ukrainian side off-guard, so that later Russia can accuse Ukraine of 'not being serious' about the peace negotiations. President of Ukraine, however, later accepted the ceasefire, and proposed to extend the period. After the end of the initially proposed period, Russia continued military operations. Despite the fact, that the Russian MoD accused Ukraine of violating the agreement multiple times, after the ceasefire ended, Russian officials proclaimed it successful, and 'acknowledged the reduced intensity of the military activities' during the ceasefire period.

On 10 April 2025, teachers, students, and citizens gathered in front of the 'Jovan Jovanovic Zmaj' Gymnasium in Novi Sad, protesting against recommencing the school year. The protesters remained firm in their support for the students and teachers in blockades. The protesters also called for the school director's resignation, as one of the main initiators of preventing the blockades.

On 10 April 2025, citizens from several Belgrade municipalities gathered in Belgrade - Zvezdara, demanding accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. assoc_actor_1: Military Forces of Russia (2000-) National Guard; Moscow Voluntary People's Militia; Police Forces of Russia (2000-) Federal Security Service
notes: On 10 April 2025, Russian police (including FSB agents and national guardsmen) together with voluntary militia members bullied and beat up Kyrgyzstani nationals during a 'migrant raid' on a sauna complex in Moscow - South-Eastern. Migrants were forced to eat chewing tobacco and hot peppers, play arm-wrestling with the police, jump into the pool while fully clothed. Police also shaved one man's beards. Those who refused to do any of that, or those who were not laying on the ground still, were beaten up. Overall 60 foreigners were at the sauna during a raid, the exact number of people who were assaulted, and the extent of their injuries is unknown. Videos of the incident started circulating online. Following the event, Kyrgyzstani Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Russian Ambassador to the country for explanation. Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs' spokesperson stated that 'the officers did not commit any illegal actions'.
